newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin on holiday in Black Sea resort of Sochi.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin on holiday in Black Sea resort of Sochi.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin arrived for a holiday in the Black Sea resort of Sochi on Friday after a three-day visit to Germany, the Kremlin said.
A presidential spokesman said Yeltsin would interrupt his holiday and return to Moscow on Tuesday to host Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
The two leaders are expected to sign, along with the presidents of Tajikistan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, an accord reducing forces on their borders.
Yeltsin would then return to Sochi, the spokesman said.
Itar-Tass news agency said the 66-year-old Russian leader was due to spend up to 12 days in his favourite holiday resort.
Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told Tass Yeltsin's holiday was "not linked to medical necessity" and the Kremlin leader would not undergo any special medical treatment in Sochi.
He would go on many walks and, weather permitting, swim Mironov said. But he did not mention tennis, Yeltsin's favourite sport.
Earlier on Friday Yeltsin appeared cheerful when he left his hotel for the airport in Baden-Baden. He waved to hotel staff and walked steadily, getting into his car unaided.

But Yeltsin, who had major heart surgery in November and pneumonia in January, looked pale and tired after talks on Thursday with Chancellor Helmut Kohl, his personal friend and political ally, in the spa resort of Baden-Baden.

At a ceremony to accept a "Man of the Year" award from the German media on Thursday Yeltsin read his speech clearly but showed more signs of fatigue than in other recent appearances since he returned to work from illness two months ago.
